Episode 244. Ambushing the Red Plutonian Tribe (1)
That evening, a dimensional gate of the Red Owl opened in the airspace above Chatin Prairie.

“Hoo, this battleship isn't bad at all. It has a long range for spatial jumps, fast speed, and even a transparency feature... I haven't tried the installed cannon yet, so I can't say, but it must surely be excellent too, considering it was made by Amella and Dr. Qwa-ul.”
While Eltiot spoke, Luna thought he was quite an action-oriented person. He never expected that they would ambush the Red Plutonian Tribe right away.

He didn't mind, though. Infiltration and ambush were Luna's most preferred missions since his trainee days. Above all, Luna looked forward to the opportunity to observe Eltiot's abilities, still somewhat uncertain.
“One of the most treasured assets of the Alliance, cared for by Jin.”
“Really? Then this master may be hated by your brother.”
“What do you mean?”
“If you fail, returning safely with the Red Owl will be impossible.”
At that, Luna chuckled.
“You are underestimating me too much, Master. This kind of treatment is refreshing.”
“I see it as you overestimating yourself.”
“Enough talk.”

“You also underestimate the Red Plutonian Tribe. They may have seemed weak from what you have seen and heard, but be alert, my disciple. Most of them are indeed much weaker than you, but that's only in terms of pure physical strength.”
Eltiot's meticulous, though somewhat arrogant, assessment of the Red Plutonian Tribe was noteworthy. They had swallowed Drakka and nearby major autonomous regions overnight.
The city Luna and Eltiot targeted was in Bakl Autonomous Region, about fifty kilometers from their current location.
“Hmm, seeing that no cannons are flying at us, it seems they haven't deployed serious defensive equipment in Bakl yet.”
“You mean the attack would have already begun if they had, even though we are fifty kilometers away?”

“Yes, their detection ability is beyond what current humanity can match. If they had deployed first-class equipment in Bakl, we should have changed the area. However, there would have been second-class equipment deployed, so bombardment will begin as soon as we get closer.”
“Understood.”

“Now, it's time to begin our first training. Let's go! While we're going, of course, it will be movement technique training. Merely running fast and robustly is not skill. Disciple, you must learn to handle your power gracefully.”
Eltiot stepped five times, speaking as he moved smoothly forward like a skater gliding over water.
“Try to run without leaving a footprint until we enter enemy territory.”
"That's enough, it's not hard."
Luna immediately followed Eltiot's movement technique.
"Not bad at all. From now on, keep increasing your speed, but keep your breathing calm. You must run gracefully and flexibly."
Luna began to overtake Eltiot.
She was fast enough that even most superhumans would find her difficult to catch, but it still felt disappointing compared to her maximum speed.
‘Breathing is the biggest problem. It's not easy to concentrate on the movement technique while paying attention to this.’
Breath.
Eltiot had been continually pointing out Luna's biggest problem as her breathing. For her, understanding what it meant to breathe calmly was not easy.
Isn't it just about breathing evenly and quietly? Whenever Luna thought like that, Eltiot would scold her like a ghost.

"You already possess a powerful aura, even surpassing your father's. That power is always fluctuating inside you. It's inaudible to human ears, but every time you exhale, a volcano explodes within your body."
Eltiot said, matching her speed.
"Oh, finally you're explaining about breathing in a way I can understand."

"I told you because it was frustrating that you still couldn't realize it even though we're about to go into real combat soon. Calm down the energy that fluctuates with your breath. That's the basis for using your sword like the wind."
Naturally, changing a lifelong habit is not an easy task.
But having received a specific clue for the first time, Luna concentrated on forming an image as she ran. She pictured the fierce aura inside her body calming down like a lake.
Then a mysterious feeling came over her senses. Suddenly, her body felt smaller, and time seemed to flow slowly.
At that moment, Eltiot yelled out.
The enemy's defense equipment installed in the Bakl Autonomous District had started operating. A red beam had already fallen somewhere.
The beam fell right next to Luna, and a stone from the exploding ground struck Luna's shoulder.
"Have you forgotten? This is enemy territory. If you get lost in training and let your guard down, what will happen?"
For Luna, the stone's strike was not even recognized as a 'crisis.' Even a direct hit would hardly cause a micro shock, so she ignored it, but Eltiot thought that was exactly Luna's problem.

"You might find it comfortable to just push forward with your robust physique even in a battlefield with intense artillery fire, but relying on your body to fight like that is an inferior way. You must move like a master. The enemy shouldn't be able to predict you."

Of course, Luna had so far created countless unpredictable situations for her enemies. However, it wasn't in the way that Elliot wanted. She had always just wielded greater strength than her enemies expected.

"Being strong and destructive is bound to break when met with something even stronger and more destructive. Can the strength of one person be greater than the entire enemy race in Barkle? No. Thus, if you only fight with strength, you are bound to fail today."
Shiiik, chiik...!
More enemy artillery was flying in. Elliot perfectly dodged all of the bombardment while constantly turning his head toward Luna.
On the other hand, Luna was narrowly avoiding it, due to her awkward movements and breathing, along with Elliot's nagging. She might get hurt even before reaching the city.
Nevertheless, Luna didn't move as comfortably as she usually did. She had decided to follow his training.
She was also getting a little used to it.
"Is this what it feels like to move without using strength? If I make even a slight mistake, my body feels like it might collapse."
As the two approached, a red protective shield was placed over the whole of Barkle.
"At a glance, it's a dense shield. I may have to use my full strength to break it."
If she exploded with energy, Elliot would certainly make a fuss again.
"To enter, we must destroy the shield, Master."
"What do you think would be best?"
"You'll probably say that smashing it with all my might is a low-level method."
"That's right. The best way is to use a force exactly the same as the energy that forms part of that shield to cancel it out."
"A method similar to the 'resonance' often used by fighters."

"Because of the special nature of the enemy's energy, this is something you can't do right now. I'll take care of the shield; you just focus on your mission. Cut down the enemy race blocking the way and collect the equipment."
Luna's breathing didn't falter until she touched the shield. It was her first experience of being soaked in sweat after running this distance.
Pazzeuk!

Elliot lifted a lump of blue energy on his palm. Its force momentarily tangled with the enemy's energy that formed the shield, turning a purple color before gradually becoming transparent and disappearing.
Then, a crack just big enough for two people to enter appeared in the massive shield covering the entire city.
To Luna, it seemed that Elliot had brought down the shield with less effort than scooping a spoonful from the sea.
"I'll teach you this when you're more refined and able to handle energy."
"Energy?"
"Your sibling is human and doesn't manage energy? Of course, you should do the same."
"But there are no troops waiting inside the barrier."

"Of course not. Since we haven't entered deep into the city yet, there's no reason to engage in close combat. Sitting at the control towers and pressing a few buttons is much more effective. Just like this."
As Eltiot finished speaking, Luna suddenly felt her body become heavy. It was as though a thousand-pound iron weight was pressing down on her shoulders.
It was because of the enemy's brainwave. The enemy brainwave was entwining Luna like deep water.
She could have ignored it by exploding her energy, but Luna had to choose a different method this time.
'Neutralize.'
Luna read the approximate flow of the enemy's brainwave and wrapped her body with a similar energy. It wasn't as refined as Eltiot's, but her body felt somewhat lighter than before.
Clap, clap, clap!
Eltiot clapped with a stern face.
"You indeed have talent. You can't handle brainwaves yet, but that's quite impressive. Good, let's go on until they crawl out of the control towers."
Though they couldn't hear it, the control towers within Bakl were incessantly ringing with alarms.
In the distance, a fleet was rising. The main guns of the entire fleet were aiming at Luna and Eltiot.
"Oh, by the way."
Whoosh! Eltiot dodged a beam of light. Luna had to dodge half a beat late, as she expected Eltiot to deflect it.
"I will not participate in the battle if possible."
"That's good to hear."
"It's good for you, too. Because if I participate in the battle, it means you could die."
The moment Luna was about to respond, the fleet's bombardment began. And the enemy's troops, recognizing the two people's identity, began to scream.
"The White Knight, and that writer... It's clear! They are the Celestial Messengers who escaped from Meisil!"
"Eltiot!?"
"We request the use of grade 1 defense equipment in Critil!"
"Contact our celestial brethren immediately!"
As the enemy's troops shouted, Shimat's face appeared above the bridge's window.
"Celestials!"
After receiving the salute of his brethren, Shimat smiled smugly.
"Yes... Eltiot, that old man seems to have missed me after such a long time. I will come to you now, so take good care of the two."
